correctness.rationale: The stationary no-reset probability solves the first-refresh renewal equation with g(t)=e^(−μt)/(1+Lt). Its Laplace transform S(z)=B(μ+z)/(1−μB(μ+z)) is also the constant-vector resolvent of the self-adjoint multiplication operator v+μ minus μ times the projection onto constants in L² of the exponential law. This operator is nonnegative by Cauchy–Schwarz. The denominator is strictly monotone through its single real zero off the cut, with 0<s_*<μ, and the sign of Im B excludes nonreal zeros. Differentiating B gives the stated positive residue. Upper cut boundary inversion gives the stated real and imaginary parts, hence ρ; convergence is locally uniform on interior compact cut intervals and the imaginary denominator is nonzero there, excluding singular measure there. S tends to −1/μ at the threshold so there is no threshold atom, and zS(z)→1 gives total mass 1. Stationarity makes the same survival law the backward reset-age tail. Exponential age mixing produces the stated normalized Laplace densities. The gap between δ and μ implies the continuum remainder is little-o of the pole density; averaging inverse rates gives S(0)<1/δ strictly and E[X²]=2DS(0). The logarithmic expansion of E₁ gives the stated slow-refresh scalings, including the tiny pole weight. Independent finite integration matched normalization, the survival resolvent and illustrative numerical rates at three refresh values.
